newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Yen-denominated Tokyo gold futures ended narrowly mixed on Monday, as the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar offset a moderate rise in gold prices in Friday's New York, traders said.
Activity was lacklustre with most private investors retreating to the sidelines due to static yen-based gold price over the past week.
Gold prices ranged from three yen per gram lower to three yen higher. Benchmark February was up one yen at 1,381 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $351.80/352.20 per ounce at 0723 GMT, against $352.60/353.10 in New York on Friday.
Spot gold in the bullion market edged lower late in the day, weighed down by moderate selling pressure from overseas investors, the traders said.

The focus was on the Federal Open Market Committte (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, with traders hoping that some fund money will flow to the gold market, depending on the response of U.S. stocks and bonds after the FOMC.
All platinum futures ended in positive territory, while palladium futures were mixed.
In palladium futures, buying by trade houses was countered by private investors' short-covering, the traders said.

"I think further gains in platinum prices will be limited on a lack of fresh factors, while palladium has more room to rise if the suspension of Russian exports to Japan is prolonged further," one official of a bullion house said.
A Russian precious metals official said on Friday it was unclear when talks on 1997 palladium supply contracts with Japan would begin or when deliveries would start.

Most-active benchmark February platinum was up two yen per gram at 1,465 yen. Benchmark February palladium ended up seven yen per gram at 570 yen. Silver futures were weaker. Benchmark February silver was off 1.7 yen per 10 grams at 204.3 yen.
